about: Documented client facilities for scripts/source-guard.mjs (hub #3104). The shipped desktop client reaches project files, Issues, sessions and rsi state only through rsid. Each entry below is the one narrow exception: a file, a rule, how many uses and why it is not file or state access. A new use needs an entry with a reason; an entry nothing uses fails the check as stale.

facilities.reason: Finds the rsid socket: RSI_DAEMON_SOCKET, else HOME or USERPROFILE. It names where to connect; nothing is read from that path.
Builds the default socket path ~/.rsi/daemon.sock for the JSON-RPC connection. The client only connects to it, as the TUI does; it opens no rsi state file.
Hands a checked absolute http(s) URL to the platform opener (open, xdg-open, rundll32) as one argument with no shell; the TUI has the same best-effort opener.
Start rsid (local #232) reads HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to find where the installer put the rsid launchd agent or systemd user unit; it names a path, it reads nothing there.
Start rsid checks that the installed rsid service file (dev.rsi.rsid.plist or rsid.service) and systemctl exist before offering the button; it opens and reads none of them.
Start rsid asks the OS service manager (/bin/launchctl or systemctl --user) to start the already-installed rsid service with a fixed argv and no shell; the desktop never runs rsid itself.
The terminal overlay picks the user's login shell (SHELL, ComSpec) and home directory (HOME, USERPROFILE) for its PTY.
Checks that the session's working directory or the home directory exists before the terminal overlay starts a shell there; it lists and reads nothing.
The terminal overlay's PTY (portable-pty) runs the user's own shell, the desktop counterpart of the TUI's terminal overlay; it is an interactive terminal the operator drives, not a client file read.

tauri-plugin-dialog backs the New session dialog's Choose folder… (src-tauri/src/dialog.rs): one native directory picker that returns the chosen path as text for the Folder box. It lists, reads and writes nothing, and no dialog permission is granted to the webview (capabilities stay unchanged).
